children: Coforge shares plunged 7 percent in early trade on Wednesday, emerging as the top midcap loser, after the IT services company said chairman and independent director O P Bhatt had resigned with immediate effect. Bhatt's exit follows concerns raised by an internal audit over the company’s board evaluation process.

The Coforge stock fell to Rs 1,813.3 in early trade, compared with its previous close of Rs 1,950. The sharp decline pared the stock’s gains for 2026 to around 10.6 percent, although it continues to outperform the Nifty 50, which is down about 10.1 percent over the same period. Coforge’s market capitalisation stood at more than Rs 80,300 crore.

The company said on Wednesday that Bhatt, a former chairman of State Bank of India, resigned as Non-Executive Independent Director and Chairman of the Board after an internal audit identified gaps in the process and disclosure of information relating to a recent board evaluation exercise.

As part of its Q2 FY26 internal audit plan, Coforge’s internal auditor reviewed the processes followed for the Board Evaluation Exercise and the resulting Board Evaluation Report (BER), which had been conducted under Bhatt’s guidance.

The audit identified gaps relating to the process as well as the disclosure of information, including information concerning the performance evaluation of the chairman. Coforge said certain material information contained in or relating to the BER had not been fully disclosed to the board when the report was presented.
Following the findings, the board raised concerns with Bhatt and sought his explanation. Bhatt maintained that he had acted in good faith during the evaluation exercise.

However, he resigned on September 8 before the board had completed its review of his explanation or reached a final decision on the matter. In his resignation communication, Bhatt said continuing on the board amid the disagreement over his actions in the evaluation process would not be conducive to its effective functioning.

Coforge accepted his resignation with immediate effect, following which Bhatt also ceased to be a member of all board committees. The company said there were no other material reasons for his departure apart from the matters arising from the internal audit and subsequent board review.
Coforge has appointed Vivek Sharma, currently a Non-Executive Independent Director, as interim Chairperson of the board until January 31, 2027.
